info.title: Cruise Itinerary Data API
info.summary: Cruise reference data, weekly fares, itineraries on the calendar, port traffic and a change feed.
info.description:
Reference data and weekly fare snapshots for cruise lines, ships, ports and sailings, refreshed every Monday. Fares are snapshots from an inventory feed, not live bookable prices. A null fare means the cabin is not offered or is sold out; the feed does not distinguish.

**Authentication.** Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key: <key>`. Every endpoint needs a key, and a Free key costs nothing but an email address. A request without one gets 401 `key_required`. A malformed, unknown or revoked key is a 401, never a silent downgrade.

**Plans.** Each endpoint lists the lowest plan that can call it in `x-required-plan`. Rate limits are per minute and some plans have a monthly call quota; both are reported in response headers. See /pricing for the current numbers.

**Envelope.** Single objects come back as `{"data": {...}, "meta": {...}}`, lists as `{"data": [...], "meta": {as_of, page, per_page, total, has_more}}`, errors as `{"error": {status, code, message}}`. Every key is always present; absent values are null. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Money is whole US dollars.

**Ids.** Lines, ships, ports, destinations, regions and cruises use slugs. Sailings use their integer id.

**Caching.** Anonymous responses from open endpoints are cacheable for an hour and carry an ETag. Everything keyed is `private, no-store`.

**Counting.** A keyed request that returns 2xx counts toward the monthly quota; errors do not.

get.description: Name, version and links. Useful as a connectivity check for your key.
How fresh the data is and how much of it there is. Inventory is reloaded once a week; `next_scheduled_load` says when.
Every cruise line, alphabetical, with how many ships and upcoming sailings each has.
One line by slug.
Ships, alphabetical. `q` matches part of the name or an exact IMO number.
One ship by slug.
Ports and scenic stops. Use `has_calls=true` for ports a ship is scheduled to visit. For matching free text to a port, use `/v1/resolve`.

parameters.name: has_calls
parameters.description: true: only ports with scheduled calls; false: only those without.

get.description: One port by slug. The numeric id of a port that was merged into another also works and returns the surviving port, with `meta.resolved_from` set to the id you sent.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Port slug, or the numeric id of a merged legacy port.

get.description: Destinations with their region and a representative coordinate.
The 18 top-level regions.

Match free text such as "Port Canaveral, Florida" or "Royal Caribbean Symphony of the Seas" to ports, ships and lines. Returns up to five candidates, best first. Confidence is 1.0 for an exact name, about 0.9 to 0.97 after normalising accents, punctuation, country suffixes and aliases, and 0.85 or less for approximate matches. For many names at once, use the POST form.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The text to match, up to 120 characters.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Restrict to one kind of entity.

post.description: Up to 100 items per request. The response holds one entry per item, in order, each with its own candidate list.

get.description: The all-lines Cruise Price Index plus the eight largest lines, for cabin `any` and segment `all`, over the last 12 loads. Ordered all lines first, then by line name, oldest load first. The series starts on 2026-09-06 at 100.

Upcoming sailings with their latest fares. Fares are weekly snapshots from the inventory feed, not live bookable prices. `port` matches sailings that call at a port (itinerary days), `embark_port` the departure port. `from` and `to` bound the departure date.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Port slug; sailings that call there.

parameters.name: max_estimated_days
parameters.description: Most itinerary days with an estimated date; 0 keeps only sailings whose every day is exact.

parameters.name: cabin
parameters.description: Restrict to sailings with a fare in this cabin; also the cabin `max_fare` and `sort=fare` use.

parameters.name: max_fare
parameters.description: Highest fare in USD (in `cabin`, or in any cabin when `cabin` is absent).

cruise.title: 7 Night Eastern Caribbean Amber Cove and Key West

get.description: One sailing with its day-by-day itinerary. Embark and disembark days are exact, and so is every day where the cruise line publishes its itinerary; other days in between are estimated and labelled so.
Every weekly snapshot of the sailing's four fares, oldest first. History starts on 2026-09-06 and continues after the sailing departs.
A cruise is the product (title, ship, ordered stops); a sailing is one departure of it. Cruise slugs are permanent.
Where a ship is on each day: one row per stop, with sea days. When sailings overlap, the shortest one that covers a day owns it. Window limit: 400 days; default 90 days from today.

Ships, lower berths and turnarounds per day. Only days with at least one ship appear; a missing day has none. Window limit: 730 days; default 90 days from today. Berths count lower-berth capacity; real headcount runs 10 to 20 percent higher.
The counts for one day plus the ships behind them. A day with no ships returns zero counts and an empty `calls` list.

What changed between consecutive weekly loads: fare moves per cabin, cabins appearing or vanishing, sailings added or removed, itineraries swapped, port days moved or confirmed. Newest load first. `kind` takes a comma-separated list.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Comma-separated: price_drop, price_rise, cabin_unavailable, cabin_available, sailing_added, sailing_removed, itinerary_changed, schedule_changed.

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: Port slug; sailings that call there.

get.description: The full series for one line, cabin, segment and weighting, oldest first. `line` is a slug, or omitted (or `all`) for all lines. `weighting=berth` weights each sailing by its ship's lower berths (passengers per sailing) instead of counting each sailing once. Rows exist only where at least 30 sailings matched.

parameters.name: segment
parameters.description: all (default), w000_090, w091_180, w181_365, w366_plus, a sail quarter like q2027_1, or size_intimate, size_small, size_medium, size_large, size_mega.

get.description: The last eight weekly bulk files, as gzipped CSV, with row counts and SHA-256 checksums. Column names match the API and ids are slugs, so files join to the `identity-*` files. `access: free` files (the `identity-*` files) download with any key; the rest need Platform.
Streams one gzipped CSV. `date` may be `latest`. Files named `identity-*` (lines, ships, ports, destinations, regions) come with every plan, Free included; the rest need Platform.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Export date from the listing, or latest.

post.summary: Change events after a weekly load
post.description:
Business plans and above can subscribe an HTTPS URL from the dashboard, with optional kind, ship, line and port filters. After each weekly load we POST the matching change events, up to 1,000 per delivery (`page` of `pages`). Respond with any 2xx within 10 seconds. Otherwise we retry after 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2, 6, 12 and 24 hours, and 24 hours again (8 attempts), then mark the delivery failed; an endpoint with 20 consecutive failed deliveries is disabled. URLs that resolve to private, loopback or link-local addresses are refused.

`X-CI-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` where `v1 = HMAC_SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw request body>")`, hex encoded, using the endpoint secret shown in the dashboard. Reject requests whose timestamp is far from your clock. The dashboard's "send test" delivers a `ping` with an empty `events` list.

Date of the latest inventory load the response reflects.

total.description: Rows matching the query across all pages.

has_more.description: True when a later page exists.

message.description: Human-readable explanation; safe to show to a developer, not a stable string to match on.

required_plan.description: Present on plan_required and key_required: the lowest plan that can call the endpoint.

Fares.description: Lowest fare in whole US dollars per cabin class. null means the cabin is not offered or is sold out; the feed does not say which.

oneOf.description: IMO number, 7 digits.
MMSI, 9 digits.
Lower-berth capacity. Real headcount runs 10 to 20 percent higher.

kind.description: scenic marks a stretch of cruising the feed lists as a stop, such as a glacier; transit marks a travel leg or unnamed stop (a train, a transfer, Captain's Choice). Neither is a port call.

upcoming_calls.description: Future days on which a ship is scheduled at this port.

id.description: Sailing id (the feed id). Sailings are the only entities with integer ids.

oneOf.description: Last load on which any fare moved.
Load that produced these fares.

estimated_days.description: Itinerary days whose date is estimated (`day_confidence` `estimated`). 0 means every day is exact.

day_confidence.description: `exact`: embark and disembark days, and every day of a sailing whose cruise line publishes its day-by-day itinerary (this sailing's, or its cruise's with the same nights). `estimated`: placed from leg distances, because the feed lists stops without day numbers.

itinerary_source.description: `official`: the line's own published day-by-day itinerary (one sailing of this cruise, fetched within the last 30 days). `supplier`: the feed's stop list, which has no day numbers.

seq.description: Position in the itinerary, from 1. Not a day number.

oneOf.description: Day of the cruise the stop starts on, 1 = embark day. Only for `official` itineraries; null for `supplier`. Sea days are the numbers not listed.

sailing_id.description: The sailing that owns this day.

ships_no_capacity.description: Ships counted whose capacity is unknown.

turnaround_ships.description: Ships that disembark one sailing and embark the next the same day.

estimated_ships.description: Ships whose day here is estimated rather than exact.

oneOf.description: Percentile among this port's busy days within a year either side. 100 is the busiest.

kind.description: `schedule_changed`: the sailing's route is the same but port days moved, were added or removed, or estimated days were confirmed by the line's own itinerary; re-fetch the sailing for its new days. It covers every rebuild of the day-by-day itineraries since the previous load, nightly ones included.

oneOf.description: Cruise slug.
For itinerary_changed: the cruise it replaced.
Fare before, USD. For schedule_changed: port days whose date moved, or that were added or removed.
Fare after, USD. For schedule_changed: estimated days now exact.

segment.description: all, a booking window (w000_090, w091_180, w181_365, w366_plus), a sail quarter such as q2027_1, or a ship size class (size_intimate, size_small, size_medium, size_large, size_mega).

weighting.description: sailing: each matched sailing counts once (the published index). berth: each sailing weighted by its ship's lower berths; sailings with no berth count are left out.

oneOf.description: Mean of ln(new/old) over matched sailings, each winsorized to -0.5..0.5.
Percent of matched sailings whose fare fell.
Percent priced before and unpriced now, still listed.
Mean fare per night, USD, over the matched set.
berth rows only: percent of the matched sailings whose ship has a berth count. Null for sailing rows.

confidence.description: 0 to 1. 1.0 is an exact name match; below about 0.6 is a guess.

next_scheduled_load.description: When the next weekly load is due (ISO 8601 with offset).

access.description: free: any key, Free included; platform: the Platform plan.

id.description: Delivery id; the same on every retry of this delivery.

pages.description: Deliveries for this load; each holds up to 1,000 events.

id.description: Sailing id (the feed id). Sailings are the only entities with integer ids.

Load that produced these fares.

ships_no_capacity.description: Ships counted whose capacity is unknown.

turnaround_ships.description: Ships that disembark one sailing and embark the next the same day.

E400.description: Bad request: an unknown or malformed parameter. The message names it.

error.message: Parameter 'cabin' must be one of: inside, outside, balcony, suite.

E401.description: No key was sent (`key_required`; a free key is one email away at /signup), or the key is malformed, unknown or revoked (`invalid_key`). A bad key is never treated as anonymous.

error.message: This endpoint needs an API key. Get a free one at https://cruise-itinerary.com/signup and send it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>".

E403.description: The plan does not include this endpoint (`plan_required`, with `required_plan`), or the account is suspended (`account_suspended`).

error.message: This endpoint needs the Business plan or above; this key is on the Developer plan.

E429.description: Per-minute rate limit (`rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`) or monthly quota (`quota_exceeded`) reached.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate window resets.

error.message: Rate limit of 60 requests per minute exceeded. Retry in 31 seconds.
Internal error. Try again; if it persists, contact support.

page.name: page
page.description: Page number, from 1. Pages deeper than 100,000 rows are refused.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

bearerAuth.description: Key from the dashboard: ci_live_ followed by 32 letters and digits.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyHeader.description: The same key, as a header.
